meta.title: Heaven Is

summary.speaker: Pastor Chris
summary.bigIdea: Heaven is everything beautiful about life without everything that breaks it, and our grief and longing point us toward it.
summary.overview: Pastor Chris speaks about the longing we feel for people we can no longer call. He explains that grief is not the enemy, because it is love pointing toward eternity. Then he describes what we can look forward to in heaven.

points.title: Grief Is Love Pointing to Eternity
points.text: Jesus wept at the tomb of his friend, so sadness is a holy thing and not a lack of faith. Jesus calls those who mourn blessed. Paul tells us to grieve with hope, and Revelation promises that God will wipe away every tear.

points.title: Eternity in Our Hearts, a Feast Ahead
points.text: God has placed a sense of eternity in every heart. Pastor Chris asks us to imagine our best day ever and then multiply it. Isaiah pictures a great feast where God ends death and removes shame, and everyone celebrates together.

points.title: Explore and Create Like Children
points.text: Heaven is not small or boring. God will renew the whole world, so we can explore, serve, and create without frustration. Jesus said we must become like little children, who believe they were made to create.

points.title: Love Without Loss, Joy in God’s Presence
points.text: In heaven we will love without fear of loss, and we will be fully understood. The greatest joy of all will be God himself. We will live in his presence and in his light.

summary.takeaway: This week, remember that longing is healthy, and take a quiet moment to imagine your best day ever multiplied in heaven.

john11.text: “When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, ‘Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.’ When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come along with her also weeping, he was deeply moved in spirit and troubled. ‘Where have you laid him?’ he asked. ‘Come and see, Lord,’ they replied. Jesus wept. Then the Jews said, ‘See how he loved him!’”

matt5.text: “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.”

thess4.text: “Brothers and sisters, we do not want you to be uninformed about those who sleep in death, so that you do not grieve like the rest of mankind, who have no hope. For we believe that Jesus died and rose again, and so we believe that God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in him.”

rev21.text: “He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away. He who was seated on the throne said, ‘I am making everything new!’ Then he said, ‘Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.’”

eccl3.text: “He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.”

isa25.text: “On this mountain the LORD Almighty will prepare a feast of rich food for all peoples, a banquet of aged wine—the best of meats and the finest of wines. On this mountain he will destroy the shroud that enfolds all peoples, the sheet that covers all nations; he will swallow up death forever. The Sovereign LORD will wipe away the tears from all faces; he will remove his people’s disgrace from all the earth. The LORD has spoken. In that day they will say, ‘Surely this is our God; we trusted in him, and he saved us. This is the LORD, we trusted in him; let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation.’”

rom8.text: “For the creation waits in eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed. For the creation was subjected to frustration, not by its own choice, but by the will of the one who subjected it, in hope that the creation itself will be liberated from its bondage to decay and brought into the freedom and glory of the children of God.”

matt18.text: “At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, ‘Who, then, is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?’ He called a little child to him, and placed the child among them. And he said: ‘Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Therefore, whoever takes the lowly position of this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.’”

ps16.text: “You make known to me the path of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence, with eternal pleasures at your right hand.”

rev22.text: “Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb down the middle of the great street of the city. On each side of the river stood the tree of life, bearing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit every month. And the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations. No longer will there be any curse. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city, and his servants will serve him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. There will be no more night. They will not need the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, for the Lord God will give them light. And they will reign for ever and ever.”

lewisgrief.name: C.S. Lewis
lewisgrief.quote: No one ever told me that grief felt so like fear.

questions.text: What helps a community be a safe place for people to show sadness?
What gives people hope when they feel sad about something they cannot change?
What kind of experience, such as music, nature, or a quiet moment, makes people feel there is more than this life?
Think of a meal or celebration you remember fondly. What made it so special?
If you could explore any place in a renewed world, where would you go first?
Think of something you loved to make or imagine as a child. What did you enjoy about it?
What makes loving other people worth the risk of being hurt?
Think of a person whose presence makes you feel calm and welcome. What do they do that helps?

prayer.label: Closing Prayer
prayer.text:
Dear God,

Thank you that grief is a sign of love. Thank you that Jesus wept, and that you are close to those who mourn. Make us a safe place for people to bring their sadness.

Thank you for placing eternity in our hearts. Help us to grieve with hope, knowing that you will wipe away every tear and make all things new.

Thank you for the promise of a feast where death is defeated and shame is gone. Give us a taste of that joy today.

Thank you that heaven will be a renewed world to explore, with good work and creative joy. Help us to have the faith and wonder of little children.

Thank you that in your presence we will love without fear of loss. Be our greatest joy now and forever.

We ask this in the name of Jesus. Amen.
prayer.source: — Based on this week’s study: grief and hope, a feast ahead, exploring and creating, and the joy of God’s presence in heaven.
